sector_model: insurer (specialty P&C, excess and surplus lines); use earnings, book value, combined ratio, reserves; no FCF model
thesis: Kinsale is a specialty E&S property and casualty insurer with a 75.4% Q3 combined ratio, 26% annualized operating ROE, favorable reserve development ($57.8M in 9M26) and modest debt ($224.6M). At 383.73 it trades near 16.4x TTM GAAP earnings and 4.5x book, which is not demanding for that return profile, if underwriting margins hold.
counterthesis: Growth has turned negative: 9M26 gross written premiums -3.5%, Q3 -4.8%, property divisions -19.3% (Commercial Property -26.8%) on heightened competition, i.e. a softening E&S cycle. Q3 net income -30.7% (portfolio repositioning cost $37.6M pre-tax; operating earnings +5.9%). Expense ratio rose to 22.0% on lower ceding commissions as retention rose. Reserves of $3.32B (+15% in 9M) rest on estimates; equity fell to $1.92B after $263M of buybacks and a $156M unrealized bond loss; equity securities ($779M) add earnings volatility. Hurricane or casualty reserve shocks are the classic thesis breaker.
invalidation: Combined ratio sustainably above about 85%, adverse prior-year reserve development, gross written premiums declining beyond mid single digits for several quarters, or a large catastrophe loss; or price moving well above 20x earnings without growth.
